key_insight: DropKV turns KV-cache eviction into a decoupled per-token scoring problem, enabling near-optimal cache removal with a provable approximation guarantee instead of an intractable joint optimization.
engineering_relevance: It directly improves long-context LLM serving by reducing KV memory pressure and accelerating prefill without sacrificing cache-budget efficiency.
method: Decouple residual-output perturbation into independent token scores
Use a cone-condition analysis to prove a constant-factor approximation guarantee
Implement fused Triton kernels that avoid materializing the full attention matrix
evidence_signal: On RULER and LongBench, DropKV outperforms state-of-the-art eviction baselines at equal cache budgets and delivers up to 19.8x faster scoring kernels plus up to 9.9% matched-batch prefill speedup.
watch_item: The approximation guarantee relies on a cone condition that is empirically verified, so performance may depend on how well that condition holds in other models or workloads.
paper_title: DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction
